info.title: API.SH: Metacritic
info.description: The Metacritic API from API.SH: public Metacritic data as clean JSON. Every endpoint is a GET with query parameters and your key in the x-api-key header. Calls that run cost the credits shown (x-credits): successes, and lookups that found nothing (404). Refused calls and errors on our side are free. Docs: https://api.sh/docs · Every platform: https://api.sh/openapi.json

get.summary: Metacritic best, new and upcoming lists
get.description:
Metacritic's browse lists for games, movies and TV: `list=best` (ranked by Metascore or user score), `new` (newest releases) or `upcoming` (coming soon, soonest first). Filter by release year or range, game platform, genre, or movies in theaters. Each result has id, title, URL, release date, rating, Metascore with review count and sentiment, user score, genres, platforms, seasons, description and image. Pass `next_page` back as `page`; null on the last page.

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/metacritic-browse

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: game, movie or tv (default game).

parameters.name: list
parameters.description: best, new or upcoming (default best).

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: metascore, user_score or release_date (default metascore for best, release_date otherwise).

parameters.name: order
parameters.description: desc or asc (default desc; asc for upcoming).

parameters.name: year
parameters.description: Release year; or use year_from and year_to for a range.

parameters.name: platform
parameters.description: Games only: platform slug (pc, ps5, ps4, switch, switch2, xbox-series-x, xbox-one, ...) or platform id.

parameters.name: genre
parameters.description: Genre slug, e.g. action, horror, drama, comedy.

parameters.name: in_theaters
parameters.description: Set to 1 for movies currently in theaters.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page, starting at 1.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Results per page, 1-50 (default 24).

200.description: The data as JSON (or CSV / NDJSON with `output`).

get.description:
Critic reviews of a game, movie or TV show (or one TV season): publication, critic, score (0-100), quote, date, platform (games) and the link to the full review, with `total` for the filter.

Pagination: pass `next_offset` back as `offset`; `next_offset` is null on the last page.

Games: without `platform` the list is the lead platform's reviews, as on the site.

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/metacritic-critic_reviews

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: game, movie or tv. Not needed when `url` is given.

parameters.name: slug
parameters.description: The title's slug, the part after /game/, /movie/ or /tv/ in its page URL. Not needed when `url` is given.

parameters.name: url
parameters.description: Instead of type and slug, a Metacritic page URL (a platform or season in the URL is used too).

parameters.name: platform
parameters.description: Games only. Platform slug, e.g. pc, playstation-5, xbox-series-x, nintendo-switch.

parameters.name: season
parameters.description: TV only. Season number; the reviews of that season.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: score (default, highest first), date (most recent first) or publication (A-Z).

parameters.name: sentiment
parameters.description: all (default), positive, mixed or negative.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Reviews to skip. Pass `next_offset` from the previous response; `next_offset` is null on the last page.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Reviews per page, 1-50 (default 20).

200.description: The data as JSON (or CSV / NDJSON with `output`).

get.summary: Metacritic title (game, movie or TV show)
get.description:
Everything a Metacritic game, movie or TV page shows: title, summary, release date, genres, rating (ESRB, MPAA or TV), the Metascore with its critic review count and sentiment, the user score with its rating count, image and trailer. Games add their platforms (each with its own Metascore), developers, publishers and franchises; movies and shows add production companies, distributors, networks, cast, crew, awards and the IMDb id; shows add every season with its Metascore.

Games: scores are those of the lead platform (the one the page opens on) unless `platform` is given. TV: `season` returns that season's scores and its episodes. `user_score.score` is null while a title has no ratings yet (the page shows tbd).

`include=where_to_buy` (games) adds `where_to_buy`: per platform, each store with its lowest offer and every purchase option (price, original price, discount, buy link). `include=related` adds `related`: the best-scored titles of the same genre, as the page's carousel shows them. `include=where_to_watch` (movies and TV) adds `where_to_watch`: the page's Where to Watch block for the US, grouped as subscription, free, with ads, rent and buy, each service with its link, quality options and price.

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/metacritic-title

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: game, movie or tv. Not needed when `url` is given.

parameters.name: slug
parameters.description: The title's slug, the part after /game/, /movie/ or /tv/ in its page URL. Not needed when `url` is given.

parameters.name: url
parameters.description: Instead of type and slug, a Metacritic page URL, e.g. https://www.metacritic.com/game/elden-ring/ or https://www.metacritic.com/tv/breaking-bad/season-5/ (a platform or season in the URL is used too).

parameters.name: platform
parameters.description: Games only. Platform slug for that platform's scores, e.g. pc, playstation-5, xbox-series-x, nintendo-switch. Each game lists its platforms in `platforms`.

parameters.name: season
parameters.description: TV only. Season number (e.g. 5) for that season's scores and episodes.

parameters.name: include
parameters.description: Extra blocks, comma-separated: where_to_buy (games only), where_to_watch (movies and TV), related. Each adds to the cost of the call.

200.description: The data as JSON (or CSV / NDJSON with `output`).

apiKey.name: x-api-key
apiKey.description: Create keys at https://app.api.sh/keys. Authorization: Bearer <key> also works.

raw.name: raw
raw.description: 0 leaves out the bulky `raw` source blocks (often 10-30x smaller).

fields.name: fields
fields.description: Comma-separated fields to return, e.g. `posts.id,posts.title`. Call metadata is always included.

fresh.name: fresh
fresh.description: 1 skips the 24-hour cache and fetches live.

output.name: output
output.description: csv or ndjson returns the response's records (its main list, or the object as one row) as CSV or NDJSON instead of JSON.

records.name: records
records.description: With output=csv|ndjson: the top-level list to turn into rows (e.g. `reviews`), or `.` for the whole object as one row.

status_url.description: On a 503 for a paused endpoint: the status page, which lists open incidents.

E402.description: Not enough credits, a spend limit you set was reached (`spend_limit`), or the key's monthly credit cap was reached (`key_cap`). Not charged.

E404.description: Not found, or not public. A lookup that ran costs the endpoint's price (credits_used says); an unknown route is free.

E502.description: The source site failed this time; retry. Not charged.
